title: Chatbot vs Workflow vs Agent
brief: Three billing tickets, each needing a different number of lookups: one, two, or three. Solve them three ways and compare. Chatbot: the model alone, one call. Workflow: a fixed two-step chain (a loop capped at 2 turns with one lookup tool). Agent: a loop with all three tools that lets the model decide. Hit 85% success in 6 turns or fewer on average.

data.name: get_invoices
data.description: Gets a customer's invoices with amounts, dates and status. Use it first for any billing question.

data.name: get_payments
data.description: Lists card charges and refunds from the payment processor. Use it when an invoice and a charge don't match.

data.name: read_notes
data.description: Reads the support notes on an account, such as promised credits. Use it when the customer mentions an earlier conversation.

tasks.label: Invoice amount
tasks.prompt: How much is my March invoice, and is it paid?

tasks.label: Charged twice
tasks.prompt: My card shows two charges of $49 this month but I only have one invoice. Why?

tasks.label: Missing credit
tasks.prompt: Your agent promised me a $20 credit last week. My new invoice doesn't show it, and I was charged the full amount.

right.text: I checked your invoices, charges and account notes. Here is exactly what happened, and I've flagged the fix for you.

partial.text: Your invoice shows the normal amount and it's marked paid, so everything looks fine on our side.

guess.text: Billing questions like this are usually a pending authorization. It should drop off in a few days.

modifiers.note: A chatbot answers in one call with no data, so it guesses.

hints: Try the chatbot first and read its answers. Then build the workflow: a Loop with Max turns 2 and only get_invoices. Which ticket does each one get right?
The tickets need one, two and three lookups. A fixed chain is the right length for only one of them. Who should decide how many steps to take?
Build the agent: a Loop (Max turns 10) wired to get_invoices, get_payments and read_notes. The model will call only what each ticket needs.
explain: A chatbot lets the human decide the next step, a workflow lets your code decide, and an agent lets the model decide. When the number of steps depends on what the first lookup shows, only the agent fits every ticket.
